title: US Sanctions Are Stifling Cuban Economic Reform Efforts, Minister Says
summary: Cuba Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Carlos Fernández De Cossío says sanctions are hobbling the island’s efforts to overhaul its economy and embrace capitalist reforms. He also acknowledges that people in Cuba are hoping political change in Washington might ease pressure on the island. Speaking with David Gura, De Cossío says, “if the US eases the amount of pressure, then those transformations in Cuba can go a long way and become truly irreversible, which is our aim and in theory is what the US wants to happen.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Consumer Sentiment Falls on Worries About Prices, Economy
summary: US consumer sentiment fell in September to a four-month low amid worries about rising prices and the economy. Consumers expect prices to rise over the next year and saw costs rising at an annual rate over the next five to 10 years, the highest since May. “Despite political differences, consumers unanimously believe that the outlook for the economy has diminished,” says Joanne Hsu, director of the survey, who joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Odd Lots: Hollywood Was Cooked Before AI. Now It’s Getting Worse
summary:
Is Hollywood just screwed? The American entertainment business has been on a steady decline since the pandemic and now AI has entered the picture.

On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, creative director of LA Material, Hayes Davenport, joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal at a live recording at the Vermont Hollywood theater to discuss how generative AI is threatening the movie making business and the ways in which Hollywood is pushing back. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nor'easter Strengthens Threatening Millions Along US East Coast
summary: An early-season nor’easter will bring damaging winds, coastal flooding, high surf and heavy rain to parts of the East Coast through North Carolina to New England through the weekend, according to the Weather Channel. Coastal New England, especially around Boston, is expected to see the worst impacts, with gusts up to 60 mph, possible flash flooding and power outages. New York City could also see rain, gusty winds and coastal flooding, with the heaviest rain farther east on Long Island. Bloomberg Meteorologist Craig Allen joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)
